<reason>B offered the stronger regulatory comparison: mandatory preventive safeguards for custody, with fund-style oversight when issuers invest reserves. A persuasively established the relevance of financial regulation to major issuers, but its own investment-based limiting principle undermined its earlier blanket analogy. Its closing assertion that cash-only issuers are absent did not answer B’s argument about accommodating safer designs and avoiding unnecessary compliance costs. B also directly answered the monitoring challenge, while A weakened its grounding through the false Tether-collapse premise and unsupported claims of prudential regulation’s exclusive effectiveness.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s second rebuttal exposed that A’s own limiting principle exempted the non-investing issuer central to B’s case. Combined with mandatory independent verification, this defeated A’s framing of the alternatives as prudential supervision or blind self-certification.</best_rebuttal>
